SMTO-SCH-0001 — The time you asked for passed before the schedule was saved

GUID: 6ca215fd-9fd3-4d9b-93ca-9e911ff54d09
Slug: temporal-request-expired
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • You asked SMTO to do something at a set time, but that time had already passed by the time SMTO went to save it. No schedule was created and nothing ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO again, choosing a time at least a few minutes from now, for example "in 10 minutes" instead of "in 1 minute". The requested moment arrived while SMTO was still setting the schedule up, so a little more lead time avoids this.
  2. If SMTO asks you to approve the schedule, approve it promptly. Waiting on the approval can let a near time pass before the schedule is saved.
  3. Open Schedules and check that the new schedule appears with the next run time you expect. This confirms the new schedule was saved this time.

What success looks like

  • The schedule appears on the Schedules page with a next run time in the future.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, especially if the computer's clock looks wrong. If the work was urgent, ask for it directly in a message instead of scheduling it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • One-shot schedule creation rejected an anchored due_at that was at or before the store's current UTC time when the create transaction ran.

What this means

  • Anchored one-shot creation compares due_at with the store's current UTC time and rejects a due time that has already arrived or passed. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Anchored one-shot creation compares due_at with the store's current UTC time and rejects a due time that has already arrived or passed.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the captured request identity, due_at and current clock without silently moving the requested time.

How to fix it

  • Create a new schedule with a due time in the future (a fresh temporal request); do not reuse the expired request. Expect this when the due time is very close to now or the create step waited on confirmation; MemoryEventStore.create_event compares due_at to now() in UTC.
  • Create a new valid temporal request or schedule; do not reuse the expired request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberately new valid temporal request captures the intended future trigger.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
